envVarDesc.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL: The API URL of your Supabase project. Every request, including database and auth, uses it as the base URL.
envVarDesc.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY: The Supabase anonymous (public) key. It is safe to expose in the browser and is used to read public data.
envVarDesc.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: The Supabase service role key. It is server-only and bypasses access rules, so never expose it.
envVarDesc.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB3FORMS_KEY: The Web3Forms access key. Used to send the contact form.
envVarDesc.NEXT_PUBLIC_FORMSPREE_ID: The Formspree form ID. Used to send the contact form.
envVarDesc.NEXT_PUBLIC_EMAILJS_SERVICE_ID: The EmailJS service ID. Used when the contact form is sent through EmailJS.
envVarDesc.NEXT_PUBLIC_EMAILJS_TEMPLATE_ID: The EmailJS template ID. Sets the format of the email that is sent.
envVarDesc.NEXT_PUBLIC_EMAILJS_PUBLIC_KEY: The EmailJS public key. Used when the browser calls EmailJS.
envVarDesc.NEXT_PUBLIC_RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY: The Google reCAPTCHA site key. It is safe to expose in the browser and is used to block spam.
envVarDesc.RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY: The Google reCAPTCHA secret key. Used only by the server to verify the contact form; never expose it in the browser (no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix).
envVarDesc.EMAILJS_PRIVATE_KEY: The EmailJS Private Key (Account › Security). Used by the server to send through EmailJS. Also turn on "Allow EmailJS API for non-browser applications" on the same page.
envVarDesc.NANOBANANA_API_KEY: The NanoBanana (Gemini image generation) API key. Used to generate AI cover images.
envVarDesc.HUGGINGFACE_API_KEY: The Hugging Face inference token. Used to call image generation models such as FLUX.
envVarDesc.GEMINI_API_KEY: The Google Gemini API key. Used for summaries, translation, image generation, and more.
envVarDesc.OPENAI_API_KEY: The OpenAI API key. Used to call OpenAI models for summaries, translation, and more.
envVarDesc.GROQ_API_KEY: Groq API key. Used for AI summaries with free-tier OpenAI-compatible models (Llama, Qwen).
envVarDesc.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: The Anthropic Claude API key. Used to call Claude models for summaries, translation, and more.
envVarDesc.GOOGLE_TRANSLATE_API_KEY: The Google Cloud Translation API key. Used to translate post content.
envVarDesc.DEEPL_API_KEY: The DeepL API key (Free or Pro). Used to translate post content.
envVarDesc.UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY: The Unsplash access key. Used to search for and insert images.
envVarDesc.PEXELS_API_KEY: The Pexels API key. Used to search for images and videos.
envVarDesc.RESEND_API_KEY: The Resend API key. Used to send transactional email such as new comment notifications.
envVarDesc.GITHUB_TOKEN: The GitHub personal access token used for GitHub API calls by the profile/home GitHub integration (repository lists, activity stats) and giscus comments. Read access to public repositories is enough, and both classic (ghp_) and fine-grained (github_pat_) tokens work. Note that organizations may reject fine-grained tokens whose lifetime exceeds 366 days — if an organization's repositories go missing, reissue the token with a shorter lifetime.
envVarDesc.FISH_AUDIO_API_KEY: Fish Audio API key. Tried first when generating TTS audio. The free model (s2.1-pro-free) has an end date; after that, generation falls back to Google and Edge automatically.
envVarDesc.GOOGLE_TTS_API_KEY: Google Cloud Text-to-Speech API key. Used when Fish Audio fails. Monthly usage is counted so it stops before the free tier runs out and falls back to Edge. Restrict the key to the Text-to-Speech API only.
envVarDesc.CRON_SECRET: The password for triggering scheduled jobs, such as scheduled publishing and trash cleanup, from outside. The site normally runs these jobs inside Supabase, so it works even when this is empty. Only when you need to call them through an external service such as cron-job.org, put a long random string in the .env file or in the Vercel environment variables. It cannot be edited in the admin; you can only check whether the server has a value.

lexicon.title: Pronunciation dictionary
lexicon.hint: Replaces text in scripts with how it should be read when generating TTS audio. Scripts and captions keep the original, and matching ignores case (RLS · rls · Rls read the same). Changes save immediately; existing audio changes only when regenerated. To read one spot differently, write [ms|milliseconds] in the script — the audio says "milliseconds" while captions show "ms". Korean and English scripts have separate dictionaries; only the one for the script language is used.
lexicon.pasteHint: One entry per line as "text = reading". A tab or → also works. An = inside the text is not treated as a separator unless it has spaces around it. Existing text gets the new reading.

flow.title: Basics
flow.items:
Pick a slide in the thumbnail strip and write its script on the right. Outside the text box, ← → moves between slides.
`Generate` makes audio for this slide or for several slides with scripts at once. Audio for this slide plays as soon as it is ready.
Audio and scripts appear on the public page only after you save the project.

inline.title: Set a reading in place
inline.items:
Write `[shown|spoken]`: captions and lyrics show the first part, and the voice reads the second.
Example: `took [120ms|a hundred twenty milliseconds]` → captions show "took 120ms", the voice says "took a hundred twenty milliseconds".
Use it when the same text should be read differently in different places.
It applies before the reading dictionary, and the dictionary does not change it again.
The shown part cannot contain `|` or brackets, and the spoken part cannot contain brackets. Malformed markup is read as is.

lexicon.title: Reading dictionary
lexicon.items:
A site-wide pronunciation list. Once added, it applies to TTS audio for every project.
Longer entries are replaced first: with both `?all=true` and `all`, `?all=true` wins.
Edit it here, or manage long lists in Settings › Services.
Changing the dictionary does not update audio that already exists. Generate it again to hear the new reading.
When the browser reads a slide that has no audio file, only in-place readings apply, not the dictionary.

paste.title: Paste all scripts
paste.items:
Paste a whole talk script and it is split per slide by `---` lines, `##` headings, or blank lines.
If every heading has a number (`## 03 Summary`), each part goes to that slide regardless of order. Heading lines are not included.

voices.title: Voices and providers
voices.items:
Voices are chosen separately for each editing language (KO/EN). When editing in English only English voices are listed, and the English dictionary is used.
The chosen voice's provider goes first. If it fails, the next provider in the order Fish Audio → Google Cloud TTS → Edge TTS takes over with the same gender, and a notice shows the reason.
Fish Audio is free until November 30, 2026, with no availability guarantee.
This app uses Google Cloud TTS for up to 800,000 bytes a month and skips it after that.
Long scripts are split into parts of about 600 characters and joined. All parts of one slide use the same provider.

listen.title: Listening and seeking
listen.items:
The seek bar plays and pauses, jumps 5 seconds back or forward, and seeks anywhere.
While playing, the script highlights like lyrics. Click a word to play from there.
Pause to return to the text box. Moving to another slide stops playback.

cautions.title: Things to know
cautions.items:
While audio is generating, the slide's script (all slides during a batch), voice, reading dictionary, paste, upload/remove/history, and adding, removing, reordering or setting the main gallery image are locked.
Editing a script after generating marks the audio as out of date. Lyrics use the script the audio was made from.
Audio history stays in this browser only, up to 10 entries per slide.
Uploaded recordings are kept as they are when generating several slides.
